name: Bachelor Practical Course
description:
1) Introduction to Human-Centered Artifact Design
o	Design and Design Science
o	Delineation of Artifact, Prototype, Instantiation, …
o	Socio-technical perspectives on digital artifacts (individual, organizational, societal)
o	Incorporation of human feedback (in the design, in implementation, in evaluation)

2) Foundations of Design Science Research
o	Defining Design Science
o	Problem and Solution Space and Evaluation

3) Introduction to Human-Centered Artifact Design
o	Design and Design Science
o	Delineation of Artifact, Prototype, Instantiation, …
o	Socio-technical perspectives on digital artifacts (individual, organizational, societal)
o	Incorporation of human feedback (in the design, in implementation, in evaluation)

4) Foundations of Design Science Research
o	Defining Design Science
o	Problem and Solution Space and Evaluation
o	Exemplary Design Science Research Methods (Hevner et al. (2004), Peffers et al. (2007), Kuechler & Vaishnavi (2008))
o	Non-Human-Centered Design Strategies

5) Articulating and Formulating Design Choices
o	Foundations of Academic Writing
o	Argumentation Strategies
o	Recognizing/Motivating Problems
o	Defining Objectives

6) Human-Centered Conceptualization
o	Defining Contexts for the Artifact (Stakeholder, Environmental factors, …)
o	Methods for Requirement Development (e.g., Persona Definition, (non-)functional requirements, Participatory Design)

7) Human-Centered Implementation
o	Implementation Standards and guidelines
o	Implementation processes (e.g., Waterfall process, KISS)
o	Methods for human-centered implementation (e.g., Pair programming, Shadowing)     
o	Team collaboration using a version control system (e.g. Git)

8) Human-Centered Evaluation
o	Defining Goodness Criteria
o	Evaluation strategies for Assessment of different dimensions (e.g., Design, Usability, Performance)

9) Human-AI-collaboration
o	Definition of Artificial Intelligence (AI)
o	Discussion on the assisted usage of AI tools during conceptualization, implementation, or evaluation
o	Guidelines on using AI tools in this course

10) Emerging Topics suitable to the overarching theme (e.g., Knowledge-Guided Machine Learning, DSR for LLMs, Stakeholder Involvement in critical domains)
prerequisites: All Computer Science courses suggested for semesters 1-3.
